hints: Focus on which functional groups actually make a gas with each reagent, not just which groups react.
Remember Na gives $H_2$ from both $-COOH$ and $-OH$, while $Na_2CO_3$ gives $CO_2$ only from $-COOH$ and $NaOH$ gives no gas at all.
Count the moles of gas per mole of organic compound using $0.5$ mol gas per reacting group, then rank $1.5$, $1.0$, $0.5$ and $0$.
walkthrough:
**Recall what gas each reagent makes**

Think like a teacher: only certain pairings release a gas. This is the key to the whole question.

$$2\text{-COOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{-COONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{-COOH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{-COONa} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{-COOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{-COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O (no gas)}$$

**Calculate gas for W and Z with Na**

Na reacts with every acidic proton, from both carboxylic acids and alcohols. Each $-COOH$ or $-OH$ gives $0.5$ mol $H_2$.

W is $(\text{CH}_2\text{COOH})_2$ which has 2 $\times$ $-COOH$ and 0 $\times$ $-OH$. So gas = $2 \times 0.5 = 1.0$ mol $H_2$.

Z is $\text{CH(OH)(COOH)CH}_2\text{COOH}$ which has 2 $\times$ $-COOH$ plus 1 $\times$ alcoholic $-OH$. So gas = $3 \times 0.5 = 1.5$ mol $H_2$.

**Calculate gas for X and Y**

X is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{COOH}$ with $Na_2CO_3$. Only the 1 $\times$ $-COOH$ reacts, the alcohol does not.

$$1 \text{ mol acid} \rightarrow 0.5 \text{ mol } \text{CO}_2$$

Y uses the same compound with $NaOH$. This is simple neutralisation to salt plus water, so $0$ mol gas is collected.

**Rank by volume**

At the same T and p, volume is proportional to moles of gas. So compare moles directly.

$$Z (1.5) > W (1.0) > X (0.5) > Y (0)$$

options.A: Incorrect. Putting W first ignores that Z has one extra reacting $-OH$ group with Na. Y makes no gas at all, so it cannot be second.
options.B: Incorrect. W before Z is wrong because $2$ $-COOH$ groups give $1.0$ mol $H_2$ while $2$ $-COOH$ plus $1$ $-OH$ gives $1.5$ mol $H_2$. Y also gives zero gas, so it cannot be ahead of X.
options.C: Correct. Z gives $1.5$ mol $H_2$, W gives $1.0$ mol $H_2$, X gives $0.5$ mol $CO_2$, and Y gives $0$ mol gas. This gives the order Z > W > X > Y.
options.D: Incorrect. Z is correctly greatest and Y is correctly least, but X and W are swapped. X gives only $0.5$ mol $CO_2$ from one $-COOH$, while W gives $1.0$ mol $H_2$ from two $-COOH$ groups.
